- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >65.00), model often overshoots and fails to revert; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% and add a slight downward slope to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to short-term forecasts.  
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., +0.30+), model lags in recognizing the shift; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and increase slope gently.  
- For long-term (15+ days) forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast variance within ±3% of recent 7-day moving average.
